review.review_notes: Synthetic browser console error when an SPA static server returns index.html for a missing bundle file.

model_input.raw_error:
Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<' (at main.e829bf.js:1:1)

Browser console details:
Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 200 (OK) for https://myapp.example.com/assets/main.e829bf.js
Content-Type: text/html; charset=UTF-8

context.recent_changes: Deployed a new frontend build to production server.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The browser requested a JavaScript bundle that does not exist on the server (e.g. from an outdated cached index.html), and the single-page application router returned index.html (starting with '<!DOCTYPE') instead of a 404, causing a JavaScript parse syntax error.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Configure the web server static asset route to return a 404 for missing /assets/* files instead of falling back to index.html, and verify asset caching headers.

target_report.summary: The browser received an HTML page instead of a JavaScript bundle, causing a SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'.
target_report.plain_explanation: When your browser tried to load your application's JavaScript file ('main.e829bf.js'), the server responded with HTML (starting with '<!DOCTYPE html>') instead of JavaScript code. In Single Page Applications, this commonly happens when the server's catch-all route redirects every missing file request back to index.html.

likely_causes.description: The requested JS bundle filename was replaced during a recent deployment, but the user's browser loaded a cached index.html requesting the old file, which the server routed to index.html.
The static file hosting server (Nginx or Express) has an incorrect base path or root directory configuration for the /assets folder.

missing_context_questions: What web server is serving the static files (e.g. Nginx, Express, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages)?
Does hard-refreshing the browser (Ctrl+F5 or Cmd+Shift+R) resolve the error by downloading the latest index.html?
target_report.repair_prompt: Please inspect the web server routing configuration and static asset paths. The browser fails with: "Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<' (at main.js)" because requests to /assets/ return an HTML document. Ensure that the web server serves static files from the build output directory and only falls back to index.html for navigation routes (not for missing .js or .css files). Set appropriate Cache-Control headers on index.html.
verification_steps: Open browser Network tab, select 'main.*.js', and check the Response tab to confirm it contains JavaScript, not HTML.
Verify that index.html is served with 'Cache-Control: no-cache' so users always receive fresh asset hashes.
Check that your server configuration returns 404 for missing static assets rather than index.html.

review.review_notes: Synthetic ambiguous runtime error. Severely truncated stack trace with only internal library frames.

model_input.raw_error:
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined
    at a (chunk-vendors.js:1:342)
    at b (chunk-vendors.js:1:892)
    at Array.forEach (<anonymous>)
    at c (chunk-vendors.js:1:1240)

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The error occurred inside a minified third-party chunk (chunk-vendors.js), but all application source frames and property names were stripped during minification.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Do not guess the root cause from minified vendor traces; inspect the non-minified error in local development or upload source maps to error tracking to identify the original file and line.

target_report.summary: Production JavaScript crashed with a TypeError, but the stack trace is completely minified and missing application context.
target_report.plain_explanation: The error message indicates that code tried to access a property on an undefined variable, but because this happened in production minified code ('chunk-vendors.js'), function names ('a', 'b', 'c') and file paths have been replaced by short abbreviations. From this snippet alone, it is impossible to know which application component or data structure caused the failure.

likely_causes.description: An application component passed unexpected data (such as null or undefined) to a vendor library function.
A vendor library encountered an unhandled edge case during an array forEach iteration.

missing_context_questions: Can you reproduce this error in your local development environment where source code and unminified stack traces are available?
What user action (e.g. clicking a button, submitting a form, loading a route) triggered this error?
Do you have source maps or an error monitoring tool (like Sentry) that resolves the original component name?
target_report.repair_prompt: The production log shows: "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined at a (chunk-vendors.js:1:342)". Because the stack trace is minified without source maps, do not make speculative changes to vendor files. Instead, reproduce the issue locally with 'npm run dev', capture the unminified component and variable name, and inspect the data passed to the failing function. Provide the unminified stack trace for an accurate repair.
verification_steps: Reproduce the user flow locally in development mode and check the browser console for the unminified file name and line number.
If debugging in production, enable private source maps in your monitoring dashboard to de-minify the stack trace.
Verify that the parent component passes valid data before calling array methods.

review.review_notes: Synthetic configuration failure where an environment variable exists but is set to an empty string.

context.recent_changes: Added API_BASE_URL to deployment dashboard but forgot to fill in the value.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The environment variable API_BASE_URL is defined in the deployment environment but contains an empty string (''), causing the URL constructor to fail.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Set API_BASE_URL to a valid absolute HTTP/HTTPS URL in the deployment environment and add a defensive check in client.js.

target_report.summary: Node.js failed to initialize client because API_BASE_URL is set to an empty string.
target_report.plain_explanation: The application tried to parse 'process.env.API_BASE_URL' as a web address, but the variable exists as an empty string (''). In many deployment dashboards, adding a variable key without filling in the value creates an empty string rather than leaving it unset, which passes simple 'if (variable)' checks but crashes when parsed.

likely_causes.description: API_BASE_URL is declared in the hosting provider's dashboard or .env file with an empty value.
A secret manager or CI variable substitution failed silently, leaving the variable blank.

missing_context_questions: What value is entered for API_BASE_URL in your hosting provider's Environment Variables settings?
Does your local .env file have a valid URL (e.g. 'https://api.example.com') for this variable?
warnings: Verify that the API_BASE_URL points to the intended environment (staging vs production) to prevent sending production traffic to a test API.
target_report.repair_prompt: Please inspect src/lib/client.js and your environment configuration. The runtime crashes with: "Error: Invalid URL: ''" at 'new URL(process.env.API_BASE_URL)'. Set API_BASE_URL to a valid absolute URL (e.g., https://api.example.com) in your environment settings. In src/lib/client.js, add a check that validates API_BASE_URL is non-empty before passing it to new URL(), throwing a descriptive error if missing. Do not hardcode production URLs into code.
verification_steps: Check your deployment environment settings to verify API_BASE_URL contains a valid URL starting with http:// or https://.
Add a validation guard in src/lib/client.js providing a clear error message when the variable is missing or blank.
Restart the process and verify that createBackendClient initializes without throwing an Invalid URL error.

review.review_notes: Synthetic build failure when environment Node version does not satisfy package.json engines field.

context.recent_changes: Running build in a CI pipeline using an older container image.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The CI runner is executing Node v18.17.0, but package.json specifies an engines requirement of '>=20.0.0', causing npm to fail with EBADENGINE.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Upgrade the Node.js version in the CI runner or .nvmrc to Node 20 LTS or newer, or adjust the engines constraint if Node 18 is intentionally supported.

target_report.summary: npm install stopped with EBADENGINE because the active Node.js version (v18.17.0) is older than the required version (>=20.0.0).
target_report.plain_explanation: Your project's package.json declares that it requires Node.js version 20 or higher. The environment where this command ran is using Node.js v18.17.0. npm halted the installation because older Node versions may lack required JavaScript features or runtime APIs needed by the project.

likely_causes.description: The CI runner, deployment platform, or local terminal is using an outdated Node.js runtime (v18) instead of Node 20 LTS.
A recent package.json update increased the required 'engines.node' field without updating the deployment server configuration.

missing_context_questions: Can you upgrade the Node.js runtime in your CI/hosting environment to the current LTS version (v20 or v22)?
Does your repository contain a '.nvmrc' or '.node-version' file specifying the target Node version?
target_report.repair_prompt: Please inspect package.json engines field and your environment runtime. The build fails with: "npm ERR! code EBADENGINE ... Required: {node: >=20.0.0}, Actual: {node: v18.17.0}". Update your CI pipeline or server configuration to install Node.js 20 (e.g., update 'actions/setup-node' to 'node-version: 20' in GitHub Actions, or select Node 20 in hosting dashboard). If Node 18 is required, check whether dependencies genuinely need Node 20 before lowering the engine constraint. Do not use --engine-strict bypasses.
verification_steps: Run 'node -v' in your build environment and verify it reports v20.x.x or higher.
Run 'npm install' in the updated environment and verify it completes without EBADENGINE warnings.
Commit a '.nvmrc' file containing '20' to ensure consistent runtime versions across team members.

review.review_notes: Synthetic React runtime failure when rendering an object directly into JSX.

model_input.raw_error:
Error: Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {id, name, email}). If you meant to render a collection of children, use an array instead.
    at throwOnInvalidObjectType (react-dom.development.js:14887:9)
    at reconcileChildFibers (react-dom.development.js:15824:14)
    at UserCard (src/components/UserCard.jsx:8:5)

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The component attempts to render the entire 'user' object directly inside JSX ({user}) instead of rendering a specific string or property like {user.name}.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Render primitive properties such as {user.name} or JSON.stringify(user) instead of the raw object.

target_report.summary: React threw an error because UserCard attempted to render an object directly into JSX.
target_report.plain_explanation: In React, you can only render text strings, numbers, or other React components inside JSX tags. When you write '{user}', React sees an object like '{ id, name, email }' and does not know which field to show on screen, so it stops with an error.

likely_causes.description: The UserCard component placed the raw 'user' object inside JSX ({user}) instead of accessing a property like {user.name}.
A function or hook returned an object when the component expected a string or JSX element.

missing_context_questions: Which property of the 'user' object (e.g. user.name, user.email) did you intend to display inside the card?
Is 'user' expected to be a single object or an array of objects to iterate over?
target_report.repair_prompt:
Please inspect src/components/UserCard.jsx around line 8. React throws: "Error: Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {id, name, email})". Replace the raw '{user}' object reference with specific properties to display (for example, '

{user.name}

{user.email}

'). Do not change component props or outer card styling.
verification_steps: Verify that UserCard renders primitive properties (e.g. user.name) rather than the raw object reference.
Reload the page in your browser and confirm that UserCard displays the user details without crashing.
Test with an empty or missing user object to ensure fallback behavior is handled gracefully.

review.review_notes: Synthetic git merge conflict markers left inside package-lock.json.

model_input.raw_error:
npm ERR! code EJSONPARSE
npm ERR! path /workspace/package-lock.json
npm ERR! JSON.parse Failed to parse json
npm ERR! Unexpected token '<' (0x3C) in JSON at position 1482 while parsing near '..."name": "app",\n<<<<<<< HEAD\n  "version...'

context.recent_changes: Merged main branch into feature branch using git merge.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: Git merge conflict markers ('<<<<<<< HEAD', '=======', '>>>>>>>') were saved inside package-lock.json, making it invalid JSON.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Delete the corrupted package-lock.json and regenerate it cleanly by running 'npm install'.

target_report.summary: npm install failed because package-lock.json contains unresolved Git merge conflict markers.
target_report.plain_explanation: During a git merge, git inserted conflict markers (like '<<<<<<< HEAD' and '=======') directly into 'package-lock.json'. Because JSON does not allow merge markers, npm fails to parse the file.

likely_causes.description: A git merge conflict occurred on package-lock.json and the conflict markers were committed or left in the working copy.
A manual text edit corrupted the JSON structure of package-lock.json.

missing_context_questions: Did you recently resolve a git merge conflict between branches?
Is package.json itself valid JSON and conflict-free?
target_report.repair_prompt: Please inspect package-lock.json. npm reports: "Unexpected token '<' in JSON ... <<<<<<< HEAD". Ensure package.json has no conflict markers, delete the corrupted lockfile ('rm package-lock.json'), and run 'npm install' to let npm generate a clean, conflict-free package-lock.json. Do not manually edit large lockfile diffs.
verification_steps: Delete the corrupted package-lock.json.
Run 'npm install' to generate a fresh package-lock.json.
Verify 'git status' shows a clean, valid package-lock.json.

review.review_notes: Synthetic React crash when dangerouslySetInnerHTML is passed null or non-object.

model_input.raw_error:
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '__html')
    at setInitialDOMProperties (react-dom.development.js:9644:28)
    at setInitialProperties (react-dom.development.js:9852:5)
    at MarkdownPreview (src/components/MarkdownPreview.jsx:11:7)

context.code_excerpt: <div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={renderedContent} /> // line 11, where renderedContent is null initially

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The prop dangerouslySetInnerHTML expects an object of the exact shape { __html: string }, but null was passed.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Pass an object { __html: renderedContent || '' } or guard rendering with conditional check.

target_report.summary: MarkdownPreview crashed because dangerouslySetInnerHTML was passed null instead of { __html: ... }.
target_report.plain_explanation: In React, 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML' strictly requires an object with an '__html' property (e.g. '{ __html: htmlString }'). Passing 'null' or undefined causes React's internal DOM property setter to crash when attempting to read 'null.__html'.

likely_causes.description: The variable passed to dangerouslySetInnerHTML is null instead of an object with an '__html' property.
The HTML content is loaded asynchronously and starts in a null initial state.

missing_context_questions: How is 'renderedContent' initialized in MarkdownPreview.jsx?
Does the markdown parser return raw HTML string or an object?
target_report.repair_prompt: Please inspect src/components/MarkdownPreview.jsx around line 11. React throws: "Cannot read properties of null (reading '__html')". Update the prop to always pass an object: 'dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: renderedContent || "" }}'. If using an external markdown parser, ensure it sanitizes untrusted user inputs before rendering to prevent XSS vulnerabilities.
verification_steps: Verify dangerouslySetInnerHTML receives '{ __html: renderedContent || "" }'.
Test rendering MarkdownPreview with initial null or empty state.
Confirm preview renders formatted content without React runtime crashes.

review.review_notes: Synthetic configuration failure where unescaped dollar sign in password is expanded as variable.

model_input.raw_error:
PrismaClientInitializationError: 
Invalid `prisma.user.findMany()` invocation:
Can't reach database server at `db.project.supabase.co:5432`
Please make sure your database server is running at `db.project.supabase.co:5432`.
Original error: password authentication failed for user "postgres"

context.recent_changes: Generated a strong database password containing '$' and updated DATABASE_URL in .env.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The database password in .env contains an unescaped '$' character. Libraries like dotenv-expand or shell environments parse '$' as variable interpolation, truncating or modifying the password.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Escape the dollar sign as '\$' in .env or URL-encode special characters in the connection string.

target_report.summary: Database connection failed with 'password authentication failed' due to unescaped '$' character in .env.
target_report.plain_explanation: Your database password contains a dollar sign ('$'). In environment files parsed with 'dotenv-expand', the '$' character is interpreted as a variable reference (like '$VAR'). If the variable name after '$' is unset, it evaluates to empty string, silently altering the password sent to PostgreSQL and causing authentication failure.

likely_causes.description: A '$' character in the password was interpolated as an environment variable by dotenv-expand, mangling the password.
Special characters in the database password were not URL-encoded in DATABASE_URL.

missing_context_questions: Does your database password in DATABASE_URL contain special characters like '$' or '@'?
Does your application load environment variables using 'dotenv-expand' or a framework with variable expansion (like Next.js)?
warnings: Never share real database passwords in error tickets or commit them to source control.
target_report.repair_prompt: Please inspect DATABASE_URL in your .env file. The connection fails with: "password authentication failed for user 'postgres'". If your password contains a dollar sign ('$'), escape it as '\$' to prevent dotenv-expand from treating it as a variable interpolation, or URL-encode special characters. Verify the password matches your database dashboard. Do not expose passwords in code.
verification_steps: Escape any '$' in the .env database connection string or test with an alphanumeric password.
Run 'npx prisma db pull' to verify Prisma connects successfully.
Confirm application database queries complete without authentication errors.

review.review_notes: Synthetic PostgreSQL RLS policy infinite recursion failure.

model_input.raw_error:
PostgrestError: infinite recursion detected in policy for relation "team_members"
  code: "42P17"
  details: None
  hint: None
  message: "infinite recursion detected in policy for relation \"team_members\""

context.recent_changes: Created RLS policy on team_members querying team_members table to check admin role.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The RLS policy on 'team_members' executes a subquery on 'team_members' to verify membership, which triggers the same RLS policy repeatedly until PostgreSQL halts infinite recursion.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Use a SECURITY DEFINER function to check membership without re-triggering the policy, or structure the policy with auth.uid() directly.

target_report.summary: PostgreSQL blocked query with 'infinite recursion detected in policy for relation "team_members"'.
target_report.plain_explanation: Row Level Security policies apply to all queries executed on a table. When your policy on 'team_members' contained a subquery that selected from 'team_members' again, PostgreSQL evaluated the policy again inside the subquery, creating an endless circular loop until the database stopped with error 42P17.

likely_causes.description: A SELECT policy on 'team_members' queries 'team_members' in a subquery without using a SECURITY DEFINER function to bypass recursive checks.
Two related tables have mutual RLS policies that query each other cyclically.

missing_context_questions: What is the exact SQL definition of the policy created on 'team_members'?
Are you checking if the current user is an admin of the team?
warnings: Do NOT disable Row Level Security to work around infinite recursion; disabling RLS removes all access restrictions.
Ensure SECURITY DEFINER helper functions set an explicit 'search_path = public' to prevent schema search-path injection vulnerabilities.
target_report.repair_prompt: Please inspect the RLS policies on 'team_members' in the Supabase SQL Editor. The database halts with: "infinite recursion detected in policy (42P17)". To fix this, create a PostgreSQL function with 'SECURITY DEFINER' (e.g. 'is_team_admin(team_id uuid)') that performs the admin check with elevated privileges, and call that function inside your policy. This prevents PostgreSQL from re-evaluating RLS on the subquery. Do not disable RLS.
verification_steps: Create a SECURITY DEFINER helper function for team membership checks in SQL Editor.
Update the team_members RLS policy to use the helper function.
Run a query on team_members from your application and confirm it returns successfully without 42P17 recursion errors.

review.review_notes: Synthetic React stale closure inside useEffect with empty dependency array.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The empty dependency array causes the effect to capture a stale closure over 'count' (always 0). Each tick sets count to 0+1=1 rather than incrementing.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Use the functional updater form: 'setCount(prev => prev + 1)' to avoid depending on the stale closure value.

target_report.summary: The counter is stuck at 1 because setInterval captured a stale closure over 'count = 0'.
target_report.plain_explanation: When you pass an empty dependency array '[]' to useEffect, the effect function is created once and captures the value of 'count' at that moment (0). Every time the setInterval callback runs, it reads the same stale '0' and sets count to '0 + 1 = 1'. The actual current count value is never read because the closure was frozen at initialization.

likely_causes.description: The interval callback reads 'count' from a stale closure captured when the effect first ran with the empty dependency array.
The developer intended to include 'count' in the dependency array but omitted it to avoid the interval resetting on every render.

missing_context_questions: Does the component need to access other state or props inside the interval?
Is the interval expected to run continuously or until some condition is met?
target_report.repair_prompt: Please inspect the useEffect with setInterval in your component. The counter is stuck at 1 due to a stale closure. Replace 'setCount(count + 1)' with the functional updater form: 'setCount(prev => prev + 1)'. This reads the latest state value inside the setter rather than from the closed-over variable. The empty dependency array can remain since the interval no longer depends on 'count' directly. Do not add 'count' to the dependency array as it would reset the interval on every tick.
verification_steps: Replace 'setCount(count + 1)' with 'setCount(prev => prev + 1)' in the interval callback.
Open the component in browser and verify the counter increments correctly every second.
Check console.log output to confirm 'count' reflects the latest value.

review.review_notes: Synthetic Next.js robots.txt configuration serving wrong environment robots file.

context.recent_changes: Deployed to production without changing robots.txt from staging configuration.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The staging robots.txt that blocks all crawlers was deployed to production without being replaced with the production version that allows indexing.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Generate environment-specific robots.txt via Next.js app/robots.ts metadata API or a build script that uses NODE_ENV to write the appropriate file.

target_report.summary: Production site has a robots.txt that blocks all search engine crawlers, preventing indexing.
target_report.plain_explanation: The file 'public/robots.txt' currently contains 'Disallow: /' which instructs all search engine crawlers to avoid indexing the entire site. This configuration is appropriate for staging environments to prevent search engines from indexing test content, but it was accidentally deployed to production where the site should be publicly indexed.

likely_causes.description: The same robots.txt file is used for both staging and production without environment-specific overrides.
The robots.txt file was not updated during the production deployment process.

missing_context_questions: Should production allow all crawlers or only specific pages?
Is there a build script or CI step that should generate environment-specific robots.txt?
warnings: A production site blocked by robots.txt will not be indexed by Google or other search engines. Existing cached pages may also be removed over time.
target_report.repair_prompt: Please update your robots.txt for production. The current file blocks all crawlers: 'Disallow: /'. For production, create a robots.txt that allows crawling: 'User-agent: *\nDisallow: ' (empty Disallow allows all). Use Next.js's 'app/robots.ts' metadata API to generate environment-specific robots.txt automatically based on process.env.NODE_ENV. Do not deploy staging configuration to production.
verification_steps: Create app/robots.ts in Next.js to return appropriate robots config per environment.
Deploy to production and verify https://myapp.com/robots.txt shows 'Disallow: ' (empty).
Re-run Lighthouse SEO audit and confirm robots.txt no longer blocks crawlers.

review.review_notes: Synthetic JWT signature verification failure due to mismatched signing secret.

model_input.raw_error:
JsonWebTokenError: invalid signature
    at /verify (/node_modules/jsonwebtoken/verify.js:89:21)
    at authMiddleware (src/middleware/auth.js:15:12)
    at Layer.handle [as handle_request] (node_modules/express/lib/router/layer.js:95:5)

context.recent_changes: Rotated the JWT signing secret in the staging environment.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The JWT was signed with the old secret key but is being verified with the new rotated secret, causing the signature check to fail.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Ensure all services use the same JWT_SECRET for signing and verifying, or implement a key rotation strategy that accepts old tokens during a transition period.

target_report.summary: JWT verification failed because the token was signed with a different secret than the one used for verification.
target_report.plain_explanation: JSON Web Tokens are signed with a secret key when created and must be verified with the same secret key. After you rotated (changed) the JWT signing secret in the staging environment, existing tokens that users already have were signed with the old secret. Verifying them against the new secret fails with 'invalid signature'.

likely_causes.description: The JWT_SECRET environment variable was rotated, invalidating all previously issued tokens.
Different services (auth service vs API service) are using different JWT_SECRET values.

missing_context_questions: Was the JWT_SECRET recently changed in the staging environment?
Are multiple services involved in signing vs verifying tokens? Do they all share the same secret?
warnings: Rotating secrets invalidates all existing sessions; plan user re-authentication or implement graceful key rotation.
Never use the same JWT_SECRET across different environments (development, staging, production).
target_report.repair_prompt: Please inspect src/middleware/auth.js and the JWT_SECRET environment variable. The error: "JsonWebTokenError: invalid signature" occurs because tokens are verified with a different secret than they were signed with. Ensure the same JWT_SECRET is used everywhere. After rotating a secret, existing tokens cannot be verified; implement a re-login flow for users. If this was accidental, restore the previous secret temporarily. Do not use a hardcoded fallback secret in code.
verification_steps: Verify the JWT_SECRET environment variable matches on all services that sign or verify tokens.
After confirming the secret matches, request a fresh token and verify it successfully passes the middleware.
For production rotations, implement token versioning or use short expiry times to minimize disruption.

review.review_notes: Synthetic ambiguous production 404s after deployment from missing build output or gitignored dist.

model_input.raw_error:
Production URL: https://myapp.example.com
Browser: 404 Not Found on all pages

Deployment log:
[15:22:05] Deploy completed successfully.
[15:22:06] Site live at https://myapp.example.com

Local check: 'dist/' folder exists locally with correct build files.

context.recent_changes: Deployed static Vite build to hosting via git push.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The 'dist/' build output folder is listed in .gitignore and was never committed, so the hosting platform deployed an empty repository with no static files.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Either remove dist/ from .gitignore and commit it, or configure the hosting platform to run the build command during deployment.

target_report.summary: Production shows 404 on all pages because the 'dist/' build folder was not deployed (likely ignored by .gitignore).
target_report.plain_explanation: The deployment log reports success but every page returns 404. This happens when the hosting platform deployed the repository content, but the compiled 'dist/' folder was excluded from git via '.gitignore' and therefore never uploaded. The hosting server finds no HTML, JS, or CSS files to serve.

likely_causes.description: 'dist/' is listed in .gitignore so it is not included in the deployed repository push.
The hosting platform was not configured to run a build command, so no build output was generated on the server.

missing_context_questions: Is 'dist/' listed in your .gitignore file?
Is your hosting platform configured to run a build command (like 'npm run build') after deployment?
What hosting platform are you using (Netlify, GitHub Pages, Cloudflare Pages, Nginx)?
target_report.repair_prompt: Please inspect your .gitignore and hosting platform configuration. Production returns 404 after a successful deploy. Check whether 'dist/' is in .gitignore. If using a static hosting platform (Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages), configure a build command ('npm run build') and publish directory ('dist') in the platform settings instead of deploying pre-built files. If using git-based deployments with no build server, remove 'dist/' from .gitignore and commit the build output. Do not deploy empty repositories.
verification_steps: Check .gitignore for a 'dist' entry.
Configure your hosting platform's build command to 'npm run build' and publish directory to 'dist'.
Redeploy and verify all pages load successfully at the production URL.

review.review_notes: Synthetic .env file with secrets accidentally committed to git repository.

model_input.raw_error:
GitHub Secret Scanning Alert:
[HIGH] Secret detected in commit abc1234
File: .env
Secret type: PostgreSQL Connection URI
Location: commit diff includes active database credentials on line 4

GitHub has blocked push and notified the repository owner.

context.recent_changes: Committed all project files including .env to the git repository.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The .env file containing production secrets was not listed in .gitignore and was committed to the repository.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Add .env to .gitignore, remove it from git history using 'git rm --cached .env', rotate all exposed secrets immediately, and push the fix.

target_report.summary: A production .env file containing database credentials was committed to git and detected by GitHub secret scanning.
target_report.plain_explanation: The '.env' file was added to version control. This file contained production database credentials. GitHub's secret scanning detected and blocked the push, but the secrets may have been exposed in the commit history or if the repository is public.

likely_causes.description: The .env file was not listed in .gitignore, allowing 'git add .' to include it.
A developer was unaware that .env files must never be committed to version control.

missing_context_questions: Is this a public or private repository?
How long has the commit containing secrets been in the repository history?
warnings: CRITICAL: Rotate the exposed DATABASE_URL password immediately, even if the repository is private — treat exposed credentials as compromised.
Removing a file from git history requires a force push which rewrites history; coordinate with the team before doing so.
target_report.repair_prompt: URGENT: Take these steps immediately: (1) Rotate the database password and any other secrets in the .env file — the old credentials should be considered compromised; (2) Add '.env' and '.env.*' to .gitignore; (3) Remove .env from git tracking: 'git rm --cached .env && git commit -m "Remove .env from tracking"'; (4) To fully remove secrets from history: 'git filter-repo --path .env --invert-paths' (requires git-filter-repo); (5) Push changes. Create a '.env.example' file with dummy values as documentation. Do not use 'git push --force' without team coordination.
verification_steps: Verify the new database password is in use and the old one is revoked.
Confirm .env is in .gitignore: 'git check-ignore -v .env'.
Run 'git log --all --full-history -- .env' to verify the file is removed from history.

review.review_notes: Synthetic React useEffect adding event listener without cleanup, causing memory leak.

context.recent_changes: Added global keyboard shortcut handling to the main layout component.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The useEffect adds a global event listener but returns no cleanup function, so the listener persists after the component unmounts and accumulates on each remount.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Return a cleanup function from useEffect: 'return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", handleKeyboardShortcut);'

target_report.summary: Global keyboard event listener accumulates on each mount because useEffect has no cleanup to remove it on unmount.
target_report.plain_explanation: React's useEffect allows you to subscribe to browser events. When a component unmounts (e.g. on navigation), React runs the cleanup function returned from useEffect — if you return one. Without it, 'window.addEventListener' adds a new listener every time the component mounts but the old ones are never removed. After several navigations, multiple identical listeners are registered and the shortcut fires multiple times per keypress.

likely_causes.description: useEffect adds a window event listener without returning a cleanup function to remove it.
The component is used in multiple places or remounts frequently (e.g. route changes), causing listener accumulation.

missing_context_questions: Is the component that adds the listener a layout component that mounts/unmounts on each route change?
Is 'handleKeyboardShortcut' declared inside or outside the component?
warnings: Memory leaks from accumulating event listeners can degrade performance over time in long browser sessions.
target_report.repair_prompt: Please inspect the useEffect in the keyboard shortcut component. The shortcut fires multiple times due to accumulated listeners. Add a cleanup return: 'useEffect(() => { window.addEventListener("keydown", handleKeyboardShortcut); return () => window.removeEventListener("keydown", handleKeyboardShortcut); }, [handleKeyboardShortcut]);'. Also wrap 'handleKeyboardShortcut' in useCallback to keep a stable reference so the cleanup correctly removes the same function. Do not add global listeners outside useEffect.
verification_steps: Add the return () => window.removeEventListener cleanup to the useEffect.
Navigate between pages several times and verify the shortcut fires exactly once per keypress.
Check Chrome DevTools Memory tab to confirm heap size stabilizes across navigations.

review.review_notes: Synthetic browser direct-to-S3 upload blocked by missing S3 CORS configuration.

model_input.raw_error: Access to XMLHttpRequest at 'https://my-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com/uploads/file.pdf' from origin 'https://myapp.com' has been blocked by CORS policy: Response to preflight request doesn't pass access control check: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource.

context.language_or_framework: React / AWS S3 (direct browser upload via presigned URL)
context.recent_changes: Implemented direct S3 uploads from the browser using presigned URLs.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: The S3 bucket does not have a CORS policy configured to allow cross-origin PUT requests from the application domain.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Add a CORS configuration to the S3 bucket via AWS Console or CLI that allows the app origin, PUT/GET methods, and required headers.

target_report.summary: Direct S3 browser uploads are blocked because the S3 bucket has no CORS configuration for the application domain.
target_report.plain_explanation: When your React app uploads files directly to S3 from the browser using presigned URLs, the browser first sends a CORS preflight OPTIONS request to S3. S3 responds only with CORS headers if the bucket has an explicit CORS policy that allows the request's origin. Without this policy, S3 does not include 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' in the response and the browser blocks the upload.

likely_causes.description: The S3 bucket has no CORS configuration set, so it does not respond to cross-origin requests.
CORS is configured but the allowed origin does not match the production domain.

missing_context_questions: Is the S3 bucket CORS policy configured in the AWS Console or via Terraform/CDK?
Which HTTP methods do you need to allow (PUT for uploads, GET for downloads)?
warnings: Avoid using a wildcard '*' for AllowedOrigins in production S3 CORS; specify exact allowed origins.
target_report.repair_prompt: Please configure CORS on your S3 bucket. Browser uploads fail: "No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present". Add the following CORS policy to the S3 bucket via AWS Console -> S3 -> Bucket -> Permissions -> CORS: '[{"AllowedHeaders":["*"],"AllowedMethods":["PUT","GET"],"AllowedOrigins":["https://myapp.com"],"ExposeHeaders":["ETag"],"MaxAgeSeconds":3000}]'. Replace 'https://myapp.com' with your actual domain. Do not use '*' for AllowedOrigins in production.
verification_steps: Apply the CORS configuration to the S3 bucket.
Attempt a direct browser upload and verify the OPTIONS preflight returns 200 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin.
Confirm a file uploads successfully and is accessible at the expected S3 URL.

review.review_notes: Synthetic inconsistency between package.json and package-lock.json causing CI installs to differ from local.

context.recent_changes: CI was recently re-configured to use a clean npm install without a committed lock file.

reference_annotations.reference_cause: package-lock.json is not committed to version control, so CI installs the latest compatible version (2.4.0) while locally the developer has 2.3.0. The API changed between these versions.
reference_annotations.reference_repair: Commit package-lock.json to version control and use 'npm ci' in CI pipelines to enforce exact lock file installs.

target_report.summary: Tests behave differently in CI and locally because package-lock.json is not committed, causing CI to install a newer package version.
target_report.plain_explanation: The caret ('^') in '"some-library": "^2.3.0"' allows npm to install any compatible minor or patch version up to (but not including) 3.0.0. Without 'package-lock.json' committed to git, each CI run reinstalls from scratch and may pick up a newer version (2.4.0) that changed an API. The local developer still has 2.3.0 pinned in their own lock file.

likely_causes.description: package-lock.json is not committed to version control, allowing CI to install a different version than what developers have locally.
CI uses 'npm install' instead of 'npm ci', which would enforce the lock file.

missing_context_questions: Is package-lock.json in .gitignore?
Does the CI pipeline use 'npm install' or 'npm ci'?
warnings: Always commit package-lock.json (npm) or pnpm-lock.yaml (pnpm) or yarn.lock (yarn) to ensure reproducible installs.
target_report.repair_prompt: Please inspect .gitignore and CI workflow configuration. Tests differ between CI and local because package-lock.json is not committed, allowing version drift. Take these steps: (1) Remove package-lock.json from .gitignore if it is listed there; (2) Commit the current package-lock.json; (3) Change CI from 'npm install' to 'npm ci' which installs exactly from the lock file. If the API difference between 2.3.0 and 2.4.0 is causing test failures, pin the version in package.json to '2.3.0' (no caret) until you can update the usage.
verification_steps: Commit package-lock.json to the repository.
Update CI workflow to use 'npm ci' instead of 'npm install'.
Run CI and confirm the same version (2.3.0) is installed as locally.
